C.  DISCUSSION ITEM(S)

1.  Recommendation to receive and file the Willdan Engineering updated traffic calming study for
  Claretta Avenue between 214th Street and 211th Street, and authorize staff to implement traffic
  calming measures and recommendations.

  SUGGESTED ACTION: Approve Recommendation.

  Neema Ghanbari, Public Works Manager, presented the staff report.

  Councilmember Vargas spoke.

  Mayor Del Rio spoke.

  Councilmember Farfan spoke.

  A motion was made by Councilmember Farfan, seconded by Councilmember De Paula, to
  approve recommendation to authorize staff to implement traffic calming measures and
  recommendations: 1) increase enforcement; 2) establish a Citywide speed hump policy; 3) update
  school crossing assembly signs for the uncontrolled crosswalk at Claretta Avenue and
  213th Street; and 4) implement a pilot program installing rubber speed cushions along Claretta
  Avenue between 214th Street and 211th Street.

  The motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES: 4; De Paula, Farfan, Vargas, Del Rio
  NOES: 0;
  ABSENT: 1; Roa
  RECUSE: 0;

  Motion carried: 4–0–1–0

D.  NEW BUSINESS

There were no New Business items.

E.  ORAL STAFF REPORT(S)

Joe Jimenez, Recreation and Community Services Director, announced the grand reopening of the
gymnasium on March 14; and the Easter Egg Hunt on April 4.

Steve Gomez, Public Safety Director, announced that they will hold a Junior Safety Fair on March 20 and
March 27.

Neema Ghanbari, Public Works Manager, announced that the Golden State Water Main Replacement
project is scheduled to begin on March 23; that the Norwalk Boulevard Pedestrian Safety Enhancement
Project is starting; and that Public Works staff began refreshing red curb markings.

Elise McCaleb, Community Development Director, announced that a grading permit was pulled for an
18­unit housing project proposed on Hawaiian Ave.

Linda Hollinsworth, Finance Director, provided an ERP selection update; announced a Fee Study
Workshop on March 19; and provided a YEP program update.
